title: Independent re-execution of pilot headline results (different operator/machine)
context: The Elyos Definition of Shipped requires that headline results be independently re-executed by a different operator on a different machine within the declared numeric tolerance before publication. This is a blocking gate — a reanalysis that cannot be independently reproduced is not shipped and the blocker is surfaced. The re-execution uses only the run manifest + pipeline code + the public dataset accession: no out-of-band information from the original operator. Non-reproducible results are flagged with root-cause notes, not silently dropped.
objective: Have a different operator re-execute the pilot dataset reanalysis from the run manifest and pipeline on a different machine, verify that headline results reproduce within the declared tolerance, and commit the re-execution evidence artifact.
acceptanceCriteria: A different operator (not the original pilot-009 runner) re-runs the pipeline from the run manifest and public dataset accession on a different machine, with no out-of-band parameter sharing.
Headline results (protein identifications, FDR-controlled quantities, key differential comparisons) reproduce within the declared numeric tolerance from repro-standard-003.
Any result that does not reproduce within tolerance is flagged with a root-cause note (not silently dropped or omitted).

A re-execution evidence artifact is committed to outcomes/<accession>-reexec.json (or equivalent) recording: operator, machine/environment, pipeline version, manifest reference, reproduction outcome per headline result, and root-cause notes for any divergence.
The re-execution evidence document is licensed CC-BY-4.0.
output: A committed re-execution evidence artifact (outcomes/<accession>-reexec.json) from a different operator/machine, confirming headline results reproduce within tolerance or flagging divergences with root-cause notes; licensed CC-BY-4.0.
